prospects.name: JFrog

score_rationale.timing: CMO Genefa Murphy appointed Jan 5 2026 for a declared 'next growth phase'; FY2027 brand-budget planning is forming now, and a new CMO's first marquee investments are typically locked within the first two quarters.
score_rationale.capacity: FY2025 revenue $531.8M (+24%), $704.4M cash, $142.3M FCF, NDR 118%. A $3-5M/yr deal is roughly 0.1% of revenue - immaterial to the balance sheet.
score_rationale.brand_fit: No software-supply-chain-security brand is anywhere on the F1 grid (Confluent = data streaming on Williams). JFrog can OWN the category outright, and Murphy's public thesis - 'trust, control and discipline at velocity' - is almost a motorsport tagline already.
score_rationale.urgency: Direct rivals Sonatype and Snyk are circling the same whitespace; whoever signs first locks category exclusivity for three years and forces the others onto rival teams.
score_rationale.ops_fit: MODE A: an F1 team ships thousands of software builds a season across simulation, strategy and car systems - that is a literal software supply chain, so JFrog earns a genuine in-garage technical-partner role, not a sticker.

prospects.headline_long: The CMO who personally built the Udemy-McLaren partnership now runs marketing at JFrog - a profitable, cash-rich public company - and the software-supply-chain-security slot on the F1 grid is still completely empty.
prospects.the_case: On 5 January 2026 JFrog appointed Genefa Murphy as Chief Marketing Officer for what it explicitly framed as its 'next growth phase' in AI-driven software supply chain management. Murphy is the decisive signal in this brief: at Udemy she personally architected the multi-series McLaren Racing partnership spanning Formula 1, IndyCar, NEOM McLaren Formula E and Extreme E. She is therefore not a cold prospect who must be educated on the value of motorsport - she is a proven, repeat motorsport-sponsorship buyer who has already done this exact deal once, and she now controls the brand budget of a company with $531.8M revenue (+24% YoY), $704.4M of cash and $142.3M of free cash flow. The strategic gap is just as compelling as the relationship: while Confluent (data streaming) sits on the Williams livery, no software-supply-chain-security brand exists anywhere on the F1 grid. JFrog's category - the integrity and security of the code that ships software - is the single largest piece of uncontested enterprise whitespace in the paddock, and Murphy's own positioning language maps onto F1 almost word-for-word.
prospects.why_now: Three clocks are running simultaneously. First, Murphy is roughly five months into a mandate her own company has branded a growth-phase reset - the precise window in which a new CMO defines the multi-year brand-investment agenda and shapes the next fiscal year's budget, before priorities harden. Second, because she has already delivered an F1/FE programme, the usual internal objection - 'does motorsport actually work for a B2B audience?' - is pre-answered by her personal track record, collapsing the normal 12-18 month education cycle to near zero. Third, the category whitespace is a depreciating asset: the moment a DevSecOps rival (Sonatype, Snyk or GitLab) plants a flag, JFrog's first-mover narrative is gone and the conversation becomes a defensive one. Moving in the next 4-6 weeks captures all three.
prospects.why_team: McLaren is the warm, high-probability path. Murphy already knows the McLaren commercial organisation intimately from negotiating and activating the Udemy partnership, so an introduction is a re-engagement rather than a cold pitch, and McLaren's technology-forward, precision-engineering brand identity is the closest cultural mirror on the grid to JFrog's 'secure software, shipped fast' promise. If McLaren's relevant inventory is constrained, Aston Martin is the strong fallback: it carries premium enterprise gravitas, its hospitality audience skews to exactly the CISO and CTO buyers JFrog sells to, and its technology-partner roster leaves the DevSecOps slot open. Either team lets JFrog tell a 'from first commit to chequered flag' supply-chain-integrity story in front of the right room.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE A - a genuine two-way technical partnership, not branding alone. A modern F1 team operates a sprawling internal software estate: aerodynamic and strategy simulation, real-time race-systems code, telemetry pipelines and hundreds of engineers shipping builds every week. That is, by definition, a software supply chain - and securing and managing it is exactly what JFrog's platform does (artifact management, binary lifecycle, security scanning across the dev pipeline). A deal can therefore be structured around a real integration into the team's engineering workflow, giving McLaren an authentic 'official software supply chain partner' story it can stand behind technically, plus a credible R&D narrative, plus enterprise hospitality where JFrog's own buyers already gather on race weekends. The team gains tooling and a reference customer; JFrog gains a live proof point and a stage.
prospects.deal_architecture: Recommended entry: Official Software Supply Chain Partner tier on McLaren (Aston Martin as fallback). MINIMUM THREE YEARS at an estimated $3-5M/yr, calibrated to JFrog's $531.8M revenue base and $704M cash position. Scope: car and driver-suit branding in the software-supply-chain-security category, garage and B2B hospitality access, digital and content inventory aimed at an enterprise-IT audience, a working technical integration into the team's dev pipeline, and - critically - a category-exclusivity clause that blocks any DevSecOps rival from the team for the life of the contract.

decision_maker.name: Genefa Murphy, PhD
decision_maker.title: Chief Marketing Officer, JFrog (appointed 5 Jan 2026) - verified via JFrog press room
decision_maker.bio: The single most important contact in this brief. As Chief Marketing & Content Officer at Udemy she personally built the multi-series McLaren Racing partnership (F1, IndyCar, NEOM McLaren Formula E, Extreme E). Previously CMO of Five9, SVP & CMO of Micro Focus, and Global VP Corporate Marketing at HPE. She is a repeat motorsport-sponsorship dealmaker who now owns JFrog's brand budget - approach her directly. Co-decision-maker: founder-CEO Shlomi Ben Haim for marquee spend.

prospects.opening_angle: "Genefa, you proved at Udemy that an F1 grid is a B2B pipeline channel, not a billboard. The software-supply-chain-security slot is still empty - JFrog can own the one category McLaren's other tech partners can't touch. Can we hold 25 minutes this week before a rival moves?"

risks.title: Budget cycle lag
risks.detail: A discretionary brand-sponsorship line may not be formally approved until the FY2027 cycle.
risks.counter: Frame it as a founder-level category land-grab rather than a marketing line item, and offer a short-form LOI to hold category exclusivity now while the budget formalises.

risks.title: Founder alignment
risks.detail: Founder-CEO Shlomi Ben Haim is hands-on; a marquee spend needs his explicit buy-in.
risks.counter: Position trust and security - JFrog's core message - as a CEO-level brand story, and bring Ben Haim into the room alongside Murphy early.

risks.title: B2B skepticism
risks.detail: Investors may question motorsport spend at a company at a profitability inflection point.
risks.counter: Murphy's Udemy-McLaren results are the proof case; lead with measured B2B pipeline and account-based outcomes, not impressions or reach.

prospects.name: Cohesity
prospects.ticker: Private (Nvidia-backed; 2026 IPO, valuation benchmarked vs Rubrik)
prospects.thesis: A $1.5B-ARR, 28%-margin category leader on a clear path to a 2026 IPO needs a global visibility stage now - and the one F1 entrant with an unclaimed data-resilience lane is the grid's newest brand. Move while the pre-IPO window and the greenfield team are both open.

alt_teams.fit: Strongest data-led narrative and a genuine MODE-A story, but the data theme is crowded - VAST Data (storage) and Keeper Security (cyber) are already on the car - so category ownership is weaker.

American and lower-cost, but Mphasis already provides data/cyber/AI services. As a services integrator Mphasis could be a channel rather than a product rival, but the adjacency dilutes a clean category story.

score_rationale.timing: Targeting a 2026 IPO - the brand-reckoning moment for a category leader. The Veritas combination completed 10 Dec 2024 brought the merged company to ~$1.5B pro-forma ARR, and it is actively building an institutional-grade brand for the roadshow.
score_rationale.capacity: Pro-forma ARR ~$1.5B (revenue $1.7B+) at a 28% adjusted cash-EBITDA margin, Nvidia-backed, with a 2026 IPO valuation benchmarked against public peer Rubrik (~$14.5B market cap, May 2026). Title-adjacent spend is comfortably within reach.
score_rationale.brand_fit: Backup, recovery and ransomware resilience map cleanly to F1's data-obsessed, zero-failure engineering culture. Re-pointed to Cadillac, whose verified debut roster (IFS for ERP, TWG for AI) has no data-protection or cybersecurity partner, the category is genuinely ownable as a founding partner; tempered only by an unproven first-year team's media value.
score_rationale.urgency: The IPO window is a one-time elevation moment, and public peer Rubrik (~$14.5B) already raises the category's competitive temperature; a grid presence differentiates the listing.
score_rationale.ops_fit: MODE A: an F1 team generates and must protect petabytes of telemetry, simulation output and design IP - a genuine, demonstrable data-resilience use case in the garage.

prospects.headline_long: Nvidia-backed Cohesity reached ~$1.5B pro-forma ARR (revenue $1.7B+) after completing its Veritas combination in Dec 2024 and is steering toward a 2026 IPO benchmarked against public peer Rubrik (~$14.5B today) - with no pure-play backup and data-resilience brand yet owning the F1 grid.
prospects.the_case: Cohesity is the rare combination our mandate prizes most: an established category leader arriving at a brand-reckoning moment with budget, motive and a clear strategic angle. After completing its combination with Veritas' data-protection business on 10 December 2024, the merged company reported pro-forma annual recurring revenue of roughly $1.5 billion (revenue over $1.7 billion) at a 28% adjusted cash-EBITDA margin, and the Nvidia-backed company is now steering toward a 2026 IPO with a valuation its CEO has benchmarked against publicly traded peer Rubrik (a ~$14.5B market cap as of May 2026; the Sep-2025 CNBC report that framed the comparison cited Rubrik at ~$17B). Two things make it a 1440 target rather than just a big company. First, it has never touched motorsport, so an approach now is early - we would not be the hundredth agency in the inbox. Second, no pure-play enterprise backup, recovery and ransomware-resilience brand yet owns a presence on the F1 grid, and the cleanest way to own it is Cadillac - the American team debuting in 2026 whose verified tech roster (IFS for ERP, TWG for AI) carries no data-protection or cybersecurity partner. As the grid's American flag-bearer, Cadillac also aligns Cohesity's brand with the US institutional investors its IPO roadshow must win. The IPO is the forcing function that turns 'someday' into 'this year'.
prospects.why_now: An IPO is the single largest brand-elevation event in a company's life, and the 12 months around it are when leadership spends most deliberately on institutional credibility - exactly the currency a multi-year F1 partnership trades in. Signing around the listing lets Cohesity convert a finance milestone into a global enterprise-brand statement, pre-build the recognition that public investors reward, and secure backup-and-resilience category exclusivity before a direct rival (Rubrik, Veeam, Commvault) claims the same adjacent lane. The post-Veritas integration narrative also benefits from a single, high-visibility external proof point that the merged company is now one coherent market leader.
prospects.why_team: Cadillac is the sharpest canvas for this brand at this moment. It debuts in 2026 with a greenfield tech roster - IFS runs ERP, TWG provides AI, but no partner owns data protection, backup or cybersecurity - so Cohesity can be a FOUNDING partner and own the data-resilience category rather than share it. It compounds strategically: Cadillac is the grid's American flag-bearer and Cohesity is a US company heading into a US-market IPO, so the partnership speaks straight to the institutional investors the roadshow must win, with hospitality at the US rounds. The trade-off: a first-year team's media value is unproven - Williams is the documented fallback for a more established, data-led audience.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE A - a real operational fit. A brand-new team stands up its entire race and factory data estate - telemetry, simulation, design IP - from zero, and protecting and recovering it is mission-critical from day one. That is Cohesity's domain: backup, rapid recovery and ransomware resilience, complementing IFS (ERP) rather than competing. Cadillac gains real resilience and a 'we protect the data that builds a winning team' story; Cohesity gains a high-visibility American launch partner to name on the IPO roadshow.
prospects.deal_architecture: Founding Data Resilience Partner of the Cadillac F1 Team. MINIMUM THREE YEARS - ideally four, to span the IPO and the post-listing brand-build cycle - at an estimated $4-7M/yr (debut-team entry pricing should favour an early founding partner). Scope: garage and car branding in the backup-and-recovery category, hospitality at the US rounds targeting enterprise-IT and investor audiences, digital rights, a working data-protection deployment for the new team, and exclusivity scoped to backup/recovery/ransomware-resilience. Williams is the documented alternative if a more established, data-led audience is preferred.

decision_maker.name: Carol Carpenter
decision_maker.title: Chief Marketing Officer, Cohesity - verified via Cohesity newsroom
decision_maker.bio: Cohesity's first CMO, leading the global marketing organisation. Previously CMO at Unity and CMO at VMware (where her teams drove the multi-cloud repositioning) - a seasoned enterprise brand-builder running exactly the kind of category-defining, IPO-readiness brand programme an F1 partnership would anchor. Co-decision-makers for a spend of this size: CEO Sanjay Poonen (ex-VMware) and the IR/CFO function during the listing window.

prospects.opening_angle: "Carol, you've run the brand through a VMware-scale repositioning - you know an IPO is won on credibility, not noise. Backup and ransomware-recovery is the one enterprise-resilience lane no brand on the F1 grid has claimed. Worth 25 minutes to own it before the roadshow locks?"

risks.title: IPO quiet period
risks.detail: Securities rules may restrict marketing announcements in the weeks around the listing.
risks.counter: Negotiate and sign quietly, then activate post-listing; use the roadshow period to build internal consensus rather than to announce.

risks.title: Integration focus
risks.detail: Post-Veritas integration may absorb leadership attention and budget.
risks.counter: Position the deal as the single external proof point that the merged company is now one unified category leader - an integration accelerant, not a distraction.

key_facts.fact: CMO (decision-maker), appointed 18 Feb 2025; ex-CMO Unity & VMware

key_facts.value: Cadillac: IFS (ERP) + TWG (AI), no data-protection or cyber partner

key_facts.fact: Williams data/cyber incumbents (why Williams is crowded)

prospects.name: Ramp
prospects.ticker: Private (~$40B+ pre-money; $750M raise in progress, May 2026)
prospects.category: Fintech · Corporate Spend Management / AI Finance

score_rationale.timing: Active $750M raise above $40B pre-money plus a newly opened London office converge into a single entry window.
score_rationale.capacity: Crossed $1B ARR (Aug 2025), $100B+ annualized purchase volume, profitability up 153% YoY - capacity is not a constraint.
score_rationale.brand_fit: Visa issuing-rail overlap with Racing Bulls' title sponsor makes co-presence structural; CFO-suite and developer demo match the team's audience.
score_rationale.urgency: The August 2026 F1 London race is a hard calendar anchor for Ramp's UK onboarding launch - the deal must be set before that date locks.
score_rationale.ops_fit: MODE B: back-office and treasury - Ramp serves the team's spend and settlement operation rather than the car itself.

prospects.headline_long: Ramp crossed $1B ARR in August 2025 and is in active talks for a $750M raise above $40B pre-money - a step-change of more than 25% in six months - while opening a London office, with no spend-management brand anywhere on the F1 grid.
prospects.the_case: Ramp's active $750M raise at above $40B pre-money is the brand-reckoning moment - the point at which a category-defining fintech transitions from growth story to institutional brand. With more than $100B in annualized purchase volume, 50,000+ business customers, profitability up 153% year-on-year, and a freshly opened London office targeting EU/UK onboarding this summer, the commercial clock is already running hard. The grid gap is total: no spend-management or AI-finance brand holds a position anywhere in F1, and direct rival Brex has no motorsport deal, so the entire corporate-spend category sits unoccupied at the paddock level. The single slot that fits Ramp's profile - its Visa issuing relationship and its EU/UK expansion arc - is open at Visa Cash App Racing Bulls, where Ramp can sit as the spend-intelligence layer above the existing Visa rail rather than competing with it.
prospects.why_now: The $750M raise closes a short, well-defined window during which brand-investment authority is at its peak. More concretely, the F1 London race in August 2026 is a live, dated activation for Ramp's UK business-onboarding launch - a marketing moment the company would otherwise have to manufacture, handed to it by the calendar. Partnership terms must be agreed before that race date locks, because the value of the activation collapses if the deal slips past it.
prospects.why_team: Racing Bulls already carries Visa as its title sponsor, and Ramp's renewed multi-year Visa issuing agreement makes co-presence structural rather than conflicting: Ramp becomes the spend-management intelligence layer sitting above the Visa payment rail, an architecture that reinforces both brands. Cash App's younger demographic mirrors Ramp's founder, developer and CFO-suite audience, and no competing spend-management brand is anywhere near the car - so Ramp would not be sharing the category. The August London race lands precisely as Ramp opens UK business onboarding, aligning the team's biggest home-market moment with Ramp's biggest market-entry moment.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE B - real operational value, off-car. Ramp's payments rail and back-office stack map directly onto Racing Bulls' commercial machine: paddock supplier settlements, sponsor-activation treasury flows, and a partner-onboarding funnel in which venture-backed, CFO-led companies are exactly the incoming audience the team wants. Ramp's Visa issuing partnership amplifies rather than displaces the title relationship. In return, the team offers race-weekend brand surfaces that fit a B2B audience: garage hospitality, pit-wall broadcast cuts, and digital founder-audience content timed to the London race. The team gets a modern finance stack and aligned co-marketing; Ramp gets the stage and the calendar anchor.
prospects.deal_architecture: Entry at Official Spend Management Partner tier. FOUR YEARS, to span the EU/UK build-out cycle and capture two full FIA calendar rotations through London, Las Vegas and Austin. Estimated $6-9M/yr. Scope: garage and cockpit logo rights, Visa co-activation rights, hospitality at London and Las Vegas, and digital content rights for Ramp's CFO-audience channels.

decision_maker.name: Eric Glyman
decision_maker.title: CEO & Co-Founder, Ramp - verified
decision_maker.bio: Glyman co-founded Ramp after co-founding Paribus (acquired by Capital One). He drives all strategic capital allocation and partnership decisions; the $750M raise and the Visa stablecoin card deal are direct outputs of his office, so a sponsorship of this scale is his call to make.

prospects.opening_angle: "Eric, Ramp's Visa issuing deal and the London launch create an exact structural fit with Racing Bulls right now, and the August London race is a ready-made activation for your UK onboarding. Can we book 25 minutes before the calendar locks?"

risks.title: Visa channel conflict
risks.detail: Ramp's Visa issuing deal could be read as a conflict with the Visa title sponsorship.
risks.counter: It is a structural bridge, not a conflict - frame Ramp as the spend-intelligence layer above the existing Visa relationship; the two roles are architecturally distinct and mutually reinforcing.

risks.title: Raise timeline slippage
risks.detail: If the $750M close slips, brand-budget authority may pause.
risks.counter: Anchor the outreach to the London race date, which is independent of the raise close and drives its own urgency regardless of financing timing.

prospects.name: Quantinuum

score_rationale.timing: The IPO roadshow is a once-only brand-elevation moment, and a recently expanded C-suite (new CEO and CMO) signals a deliberate scale-up posture.
score_rationale.capacity: Honeywell spin-off targeting a ~$12.7B IPO, a 27% premium over its $10B September 2025 round - capacity is a non-issue.
score_rationale.brand_fit: Quantum computing is the ultimate precision-and-compute narrative, and the Anglo-American footprint suits a British team, though the category is more halo than literal in-car today.
score_rationale.urgency: No direct quantum rival exists on the grid, so the forcing function is the IPO window itself rather than a competitor.
score_rationale.ops_fit: MODE A (developing): compute and optimisation R&D around simulation, strategy and logistics is a credible roadmap, even if not yet a literal in-car system.

prospects.headline_long: Honeywell spin-off Quantinuum is heading for a ~$12.7B IPO with a freshly expanded C-suite - a textbook overnight unicorn with a brand-elevation budget, an Anglo-American footprint, and no motorsport history at all.
prospects.the_case: Quantinuum is the highest-priority class in our entire mandate: a born-big spin-off (out of Honeywell) heading into a ~$12.7B IPO, up 27% on its $10B September 2025 valuation, that has never entered motorsport. Two structural facts make it compelling. First, an IPO is a one-time brand-elevation moment, and an F1 association is among the fastest ways for a deep-tech company to acquire global enterprise visibility and the kind of mainstream credibility a quantum business cannot buy through technical channels alone. Second, the company has just expanded its leadership - a new CEO in Rajeeb (Raj) Hazra and a new CMO in Lawrence Schwartz - which is exactly the configuration that approves first-mover brand investments to establish a public-market identity. Because no quantum brand exists anywhere on the grid, Quantinuum would define the category rather than contest it.
prospects.why_now: The IPO roadshow is the window. Leadership is actively investing in public-market visibility, enterprise credibility and a differentiated narrative, and a new CEO-plus-CMO pairing typically sets the brand agenda in its first two quarters. A multi-year F1 innovation-partner deal signed around the listing compounds the story - turning a finance event into a global brand moment - and there is no competitor clock forcing a rushed, defensive posture, so the deal can be shaped on Quantinuum's terms if it is opened now rather than after the listing settles.
prospects.why_team: Aston Martin is the fit. Its premium engineering gravitas and British identity align with Quantinuum's Cambridge-and-Colorado footprint, and its hospitality audience is exactly the C-suite and government-adjacent enterprise buyer a quantum business courts. The association positions Quantinuum as 'the quantum edge in performance R&D' - a precision-and-compute halo on the grid's most boardroom-credible team - rather than as a mass-market consumer sponsor, which is the wrong register for this category.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE A (developing). Quantum and advanced classical optimisation increasingly touch the problems an F1 team actually faces - aerodynamic and strategy simulation, logistics and scheduling across a global calendar, and materials R&D. Positioned as an innovation and R&D partner, Quantinuum offers Aston Martin a credible compute-frontier collaboration and a powerful talent-attraction halo, with a genuine roadmap toward simulation use cases rather than an empty logo. The honest framing is a forward-looking technical partnership: real engagement on hard optimisation problems, growing into deeper integration over the multi-year term.
prospects.deal_architecture: Official Innovation / Quantum Partner tier on Aston Martin, minimum three years, estimated $3-6M/yr, structured as an R&D-and-brand halo timed around the listing, with category exclusivity for quantum computing and a defined joint R&D workstream so the partnership has technical substance from day one.

decision_maker.name: Lawrence Schwartz
decision_maker.title: Chief Marketing Officer, Quantinuum - verified
decision_maker.bio: Brings 20+ years of global B2B marketing leadership with a track record of scaling high-margin businesses from $100M to over $1B; most recently led major repositioning at Aspen Technology that lifted brand preference and market share - precisely the IPO-grade brand mandate an F1 partnership would anchor. Co-decision-makers: CEO Rajeeb (Raj) Hazra and the CFO/IR function during the listing window.

prospects.opening_angle: "Lawrence, you repositioned AspenTech into a billion-dollar brand - you know an IPO is a credibility event. Quantum is the one category no rival on the F1 grid can claim, and Aston Martin is the boardroom audience. 25 minutes before the roadshow?"

risks.title: IPO quiet period
risks.detail: Securities rules may restrict spend and announcements around the listing.
risks.counter: Sign quietly and activate post-listing; use the roadshow period to build internal consensus rather than to publicise.

risks.title: Deep-tech brand caution
risks.detail: A quantum firm may view F1 as off-strategy or too consumer-facing.
risks.counter: Position strictly as enterprise credibility, government/partner visibility and talent attraction, with a real joint R&D workstream - not consumer marketing.

prospects.name: Snyk

score_rationale.timing: CEO Peter McKay has flagged a 2026 IPO; the CMO seat is also in transition (Jonaki Egenolf left to XBOW in Nov 2025), so brand strategy is being reset now.
score_rationale.capacity: Multi-billion valuation with $300M+ ARR (Dec 2024) - well funded for a mid-to-premium tier.
score_rationale.brand_fit: Developer and application security sits in the same uncontested grid whitespace as JFrog.
score_rationale.urgency: If JFrog or Sonatype sign first, the security category locks and Snyk is forced onto a rival team or out.
score_rationale.ops_fit: MODE A: an F1 team's growing in-house software estate is a genuine developer-security surface.

prospects.headline_long: Developer-security leader Snyk is building toward a 2026 IPO with a CMO seat in transition and no motorsport footprint - and the security category on the grid is still empty.
prospects.the_case: Snyk is a well-funded developer-security leader (over $300M ARR) whose CEO, Peter McKay, has publicly flagged a 2026 IPO. Two signals stack up. First, the security category on the F1 grid is uncontested, so a multi-year partnership would give Snyk both enterprise credibility ahead of a listing and ownership of a lane no rival holds. Second, Snyk's brand function is mid-reset: its previous CMO, Jonaki Egenolf, departed for XBOW in November 2025, which means brand and sponsorship strategy is actively being re-decided right now - the ideal moment to plant an idea. The competitive nuance to flag internally: this is the same whitespace JFrog and Sonatype are eyeing, so the category is a race, and whoever signs first owns it.
prospects.why_now: Pre-IPO brand-building budgets, an open security category, and a brand leadership reset all coincide. With the CMO seat in transition, the decision is currently closest to the CEO, which both shortens the chain and means the strategic framing set now will shape whoever inherits the role. The window closes the moment a DevSecOps rival commits to a team.
prospects.why_team: Aston Martin's CISO-grade gravitas and premium, technically-credible identity place Snyk's 'secure by design' story directly in front of the enterprise security buyers it sells to. If Aston Martin's inventory is constrained, Williams (data/engineering revival) is a credible alternative with the right audience profile.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE A. Snyk integrates security directly into developer workflows, and an F1 team's expanding in-house software estate is a real testbed and reference deployment. A deal can be built around securing the team's own development pipeline, giving the team genuine operational value and Snyk an authentic 'official developer-security partner' narrative plus CISO-level hospitality - substance on both sides, not signage.
prospects.deal_architecture: Official Developer Security Partner tier on Aston Martin, minimum three years, ~$3-4M/yr, with security-category exclusivity and a working integration into the team's development pipeline.

decision_maker.name: Peter McKay
decision_maker.title: CEO, Snyk - verified (note: CMO seat in transition after Jonaki Egenolf's Nov 2025 departure to XBOW)
decision_maker.bio: CEO and the owner of Snyk's IPO narrative and, currently, its top-level brand decisions while the CMO role is being refilled - which makes him the right entry point today. Approach McKay directly and offer to help shape the sponsorship thesis the incoming CMO will execute. (Egenolf's move to XBOW is itself logged as a separate exec-migration signal.)

prospects.opening_angle: "Peter, with the CMO seat in transition the security-on-the-grid decision sits with you - and JFrog and Sonatype both want that empty slot. First mover owns it for three years, right before your IPO. Worth 25 minutes?"

risks.title: IPO timing uncertainty
risks.detail: Brand spend may be deferred until the listing is closer.
risks.counter: Sign now to lock category exclusivity at a pre-IPO price; scale activation at the listing.

risks.title: Leadership gap
risks.detail: With no sitting CMO, the deal could stall awaiting the new hire.
risks.counter: Engage the CEO directly and frame the partnership as a ready-made win to hand the incoming CMO on day one.

prospects.name: Abnormal Security

score_rationale.timing: Raised $250M Series D at $5.1B and has publicly targeted public-company readiness; the CMO seat is currently in transition, so brand strategy is open.
score_rationale.capacity: $5.1B valuation with strong ARR growth - comfortably funds a value-to-mid tier.

prospects.headline_long: Sonatype is JFrog's mirror in software supply chain security - the natural counter-narrative buyer the moment a direct rival signs a team.
prospects.the_case: Sonatype occupies precisely the same software-supply-chain-security whitespace as JFrog, which makes it the classic counter-narrative target. If JFrog (or Snyk) signs a team, Sonatype's urgency spikes overnight and a rival-team pitch becomes highly compelling - the exact SnapLogic-versus-Confluent playbook of turning a competitor's sponsorship into the prospect's reason to act. Capacity is more modest and ownership is private equity (Vista), so the right structure is a disciplined value tier with a clear competitive-defence rationale rather than a premium land-grab.
prospects.why_now: Trigger-based: this prospect should be escalated to HOT and approached immediately if and when JFrog or Snyk commits to a team. Until then it is a primed, pre-researched lead to activate the day the category's first domino falls.
prospects.why_team: Haas offers an accessible entry tier suited to a mid-market budget and PE ROI discipline, and a rival-team position to whichever team a competitor chooses gives Sonatype the counter-narrative framing that justifies the spend internally.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE A. The same genuine pipeline-security use as JFrog - artifact management and open-source governance across the team's development workflow - supporting a credible technical-partner story at a value tier, with real tooling value to the team alongside the branding.
prospects.deal_architecture: Value Partner tier on Haas, minimum three years, ~$1.5-3M/yr, with a competitive-defence framing and a working integration into the team's dev pipeline.

prospects.ticker: Private (a16z, Microsoft, Silver Lake Waterman, Sixth Street, Capital One Ventures)

score_rationale.ops_fit: MODE A: integration/automation tooling has a credible team-systems use.

prospects.headline_long: SnapLogic appointed a President and expanded its C-suite the same day, while direct rival Confluent sits on the Williams livery - SnapLogic cannot cede the enterprise-credibility stage to a competitor.
prospects.the_case: On 12 May 2026 SnapLogic appointed Molly Matthews (ex-Microsoft enterprise GTM) as President while simultaneously promoting its Chief Customer Officer and Chief People Officer - a deliberate scale-up posture carrying new budget authority and appetite for brand investment. Backed by a16z, Microsoft, Silver Lake Waterman, Sixth Street and Capital One Ventures, with $100M+ ARR confirmed in August 2025 and customers including AstraZeneca, Adobe, Verizon and Sony, the company has both the means and the motive. The decisive competitive signal: Confluent, a direct iPaaS rival, is an active partner on the Williams 2026 livery, putting a competitor on motorsport's enterprise-credibility stage in front of the exact CTO and CDO audience SnapLogic needs.
prospects.why_now: Matthews's appointment created a leadership window in which new Presidents routinely approve first-mover brand investments to establish a GTM identity, and that window narrows by the week. Simultaneously, Confluent's Williams presence hardens with every race weekend, so a rival-team announcement now reframes the narrative before the competitor's association solidifies - the urgency is genuinely time-boxed.
prospects.why_team: Aston Martin (with McLaren as an alternative) places SnapLogic directly opposite Confluent's Williams partnership - turning a competitor's sponsorship into SnapLogic's own urgency argument and landing the brand in front of the same enterprise IT decision-makers. Aston Martin's premium gravitas and open integration category make it the cleanest counter-position.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE A. Integration and automation tooling maps to a team's sprawling systems estate - sponsor and commercial data, logistics, and telemetry pipelines that must talk to each other - so SnapLogic can support a real technical-partner narrative and a working integration rather than a logo, while the team gains genuine connectivity tooling.
prospects.deal_architecture: Associate / Official Partner tier on Aston Martin (or McLaren): garage access, digital inventory and B2B hospitality. MINIMUM THREE YEARS - re-architected up from the original two-year proposal in Brief N 009 - at ~$3-5M/yr, calibrated to $100M+ ARR, with integration-category exclusivity.
